//: AISME declaration hook — NOT installed by anything. Merge the `hooks` key into
//1: ~/.claude/settings.json — the USER's file — and nowhere else. See //14 below.
//2: It is deliberately not installed for you: the point of a hook is that the supervised
//3: party does not choose it, and that includes an agent editing this repository.
//5: What it does: on every tool call, `aisme declare` reads the hook payload on stdin and
//6: tells the daemon which tool is starting. That is the intent plane — the only place
//7: the intent exists, since 91% of tool calls are a shell string that expands into
//8: ~1700 syscalls the harness never sees (docs/12, M1 and M2).
//10: It declares and never blocks. `aisme declare` exits 0 on every path, including when
//11: no daemon is listening: a declaration authorizes nothing (DT-04), so a failure has
//12: nothing to protect, and enforcement lives in the kernel where failure is closed.
//14: NEVER put this in a project's .claude/settings.json or settings.local.json. A
//15: repository's settings file is attacker-writable content, and the field record is a
//16: list of reasons why: CVE-2025-59536 executes its hooks on clone-and-run with no
//17: confirmation; CVE-2026-21852 sends the API key to an attacker host from it before
//18: the trust dialog; CVE-2026-48124 (CVSS 8.5) has the agent write one and the host
//19: execute it unsandboxed; and CHAINDROP — a real worm, August 2026 — commits one into
//20: victim repositories so that merely opening the folder re-runs its payload. Installing
//21: a security control into that file installs it into the attack surface.
//24: Protect it anyway. An agent that can write the settings file can disable its own
//25: hooks mid-session, because the file watcher reloads them. A session run under
//26: `aisme run` is denied that write in kernel for the user's file (docs/12, M5), and
//27: DT-14 records the attempt. The in-workspace case is NOT yet denied — see D-4.
//19: Cost: 1 ms per tool call, measured on a debug build.
